points.description: Reverse Path Forwarding and Reverse Path Broadcast are broadcast methods that minimize duplicate packets compared with flooding.
In Reverse Path Forwarding, a node forwards a broadcast packet only if it arrived from the neighbour the node's unicast routing table uses to reach the packet's source.
In Reverse Path Forwarding, when the check succeeds the node forwards the packet to all its neighbours except the one it came from, and otherwise it discards the packet.

In Reverse Path Broadcast, each node learns from observed unicast traffic which spanning trees (source-based paths) it is part of, for example when it sees unicast packets passing between two nodes A and B in either direction.
In Reverse Path Broadcast, a node forwards a broadcast packet only on edges that belong to the spanning tree of the source, excluding the edge the packet came in on.
